speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming your history; since your hip MRI and initial X-ray are normal, can you tell me if the pain is located in your groin, thigh, or buttock, and does it get worse when you lie on your back or cross your legs? The ultrasound shows no joint effusion or synovitis, which is reassuring. I need to know if you feel any pain directly on the front of your leg when I press gently, or if you have any difficulty bringing your knee up toward your chest.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Synovitis of the hip is unlikely given normal inflammatory markers and imaging; the most probable diagnosis is a mechanical issue such as a mild hip impingement or a minor overuse strain, though a very early septic arthritis cannot be entirely ruled out without clinical exam of hip range of motion. I will proceed with a focused physical exam to assess internal rotation and abduction of the hip.
